model_note.S:
CC: I have an itchy rash where my watch sits.

HPI: 29-year-old female. Six days of localized wrist rash. Volar left wrist under watch. Pruritic with mild burning. Itch 6/10 with one nocturnal awakening. Persistent patch rather than transient wheals. Enlarged within contact area; no distant spread. New metal-backed watch 10 days ago; wet exposure under strap. Worse with sweat, trapped soap and watch contact. Improves without watch and with cool compress. Fragrance-free emollient only. Prior earring-associated pruritus.

PMH: Childhood eczema.

PSH: Appendectomy at 16.

Meds: Daily oral contraceptive; no new medication in 3 months.

SH: No smoking or vaping. Two glasses of wine weekly. No recreational drugs. Food-service work with frequent handwashing. Roommate had ringworm last month; occasional towel sharing.

FH: Sister: eczema. Mother: hypertension; father: no known major illness.

Allergies: No known drug allergies.

ROS: Skin: Localized wrist rash. Pruritus predominates. No drainage. General: No fever. No chills. No malaise. Respiratory: No dyspnea. No wheeze. No cough. No angioedema or mucosal lesions.
model_note.O:
Vitals: BP 112/70 mmHg, P 74 bpm, R 14 rpm, T 98.2 F oral, Pulse Ox 99% on room air, Ht 5' 6", Wt 145 lbs

General: Well appearing; no respiratory distress.
Skin: Volar left wrist: 3 by 4 cm erythematous scaly plaque with small papules and superficial excoriations, matching watch-back/strap contact. No annular raised border, central clearing, purulence or spreading erythema. No rash on the other inspected arm or palms. Wrist skin mildly tender without marked warmth or fluctuance; no joint tenderness.
Lymphatic: No left axillary lymphadenopathy.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm without murmur.
Lungs: Clear bilateral breath sounds.
Osteopathic: T2 left thoracic paraspinal tissue texture change and tenderness.
A: 1. Allergic contact dermatitis, suspected metal exposure
P: 1. Stop wearing the watch; use gentle skin care, emollient and a short appropriate topical corticosteroid course if fungal infection is not suspected on assessment. Discuss avoiding likely metal contact and patch testing if recurrent. Review in 1–2 weeks; seek earlier care for spreading redness, marked pain, pus or fever.

2. Reduce prolonged wet/soap contact and dry beneath accessories; review workplace skin protection and substitute a less irritating routine. Use barrier emollient and explain that multiple contact mechanisms may coexist; seek occupational-health or dermatology input if work-associated dermatitis persists despite protection.

3. If morphology or lack of response raises concern, perform skin scraping/KOH before continuing steroid alone; use topical antifungal if confirmed or strongly suspected. Avoid shared towels and explain that routine antibiotics are not indicated.
